newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down in dull trade.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended lower on Tuesday on light profit-taking in otherwise sluggish trade as many investors kept to the sidelines awaiting interim corporate results, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.790 point or 1.06 percent to 73.495 on volume of 7.109 million shares worth $3.482 million, compared with 11.882 million shares on Monday.
Overseas investors focused selling on Hainan Airlines and Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products, brokers said.
Recently strong Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere slid $0.048 or 6.01 percent to $0.750 on volume of 616,000 shares.
Hainan Airlines slumped $0.030 or 5.66 percent to $0.500 on volume of 900,000 shares. The company said on Monday it wanted to offer 100 million to 150 million A shares to fund its expansion plans.
"Some overseas profit-taking was seen in Hainan Airlines and Erdos Cashmere, and that pushed the index lower," said a broker.
China First Pencil announced it took over a local state-owned competitor without having to make a cash payment.
China First Pencil failed to trade after a morning suspension. It was bid at $0.346 against its previous close of $0.36.
Shanghai Tyre and Rubber was the most active issue on institutional cross-trading, though it ended unchanged at $0.490 on volume of 912,000 shares.
Of the 45 B share issues, 35 were traded, with 21 losing ground, eight rising and six ending unchanged.
Shanghai's A share index staged a technical rebound, largely due to institutional support for shares with a heavy index weighting, brokers said.
The A share index gained 12.661 points or 1.06 percent to 1,206.058 on volume of 287.0 million shares worth 2.9 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 50.692 points or 1.41 percent to 3,647.131.
Shanghai Petrochemical was the biggest A share gainer on institutional support, soaring 0.38 yuan or 9.22 percent to 4.50 yuan on volume of 29.5 million shares.
